title: Free Orange State
capsule: The Orange Free State (Oranje-Vrijstaat) was an independent Boer republic established on 23 February 1854 when Britain ceded the territory between the Orange and Vaal rivers by the Bloemfontein Convention. Under President Johannes Brand (1864–1888) it achieved stability and prosperity, expanded grain cultivation, and navigated the Basotho Wars, though it lost control of the diamond-rich Kimberley region to Britain in 1871. The republic declared war on Britain in October 1899 in solidarity with the Transvaal; Bloemfontein fell in March 1900 and the state was dissolved by the Treaty of Vereeniging on 31 May 1902, becoming the Orange River Colony.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Boundaries are well-documented from colonial-era maps and the Bloemfontein Convention; the extent of the state is closely attested throughout its existence.
